title: Ang 548–556: Bihagra ki Var
hookLine: a ballad with saloks, some headed with Mardana's name
tomorrow: can someone in love with God dislike anyone?

cards: Some weekends run on a cup. Who's drinking, who isn't, what's in yours, who keeps filling it.

On ang 553, inside Bihagra's ballad, three saloks carry a surprising heading: Mardana, the name tradition gives Guru Nanak's companion, the musician who played the rabab beside him. And these saloks are about wine.
So what's in the cup when Guru Nanak talks about it?

teach.h: A BALLAD BY THE FOURTH GURU.
teach.b: Bihagra ki Var is Guru Ram Das's ballad, pauris with saloks set before them. Readers take the saloks headed Mardana as Guru Nanak's words, with his companion's name above them.

The first, in paraphrase: this dark age is the still, desire is the wine, and the mind is the drinker. Anger is the cup, filled with attachment, and ego is the one who pours. Drink in that company, and you're ruined.
Then comes a second cup. In paraphrase: let the body be the vat and self-knowledge the wine, with nectar for its stream.
In the sangat, the true congregation, the cup of love fills with that nectar, and drinking it, the bad gets cut away. So that's what's in the cup.
Either desire, poured by ego, or love, poured in good company.
The Sikh code of conduct asks Sikhs to stay away from alcohol and intoxicants, and these saloks go one step further back. They ask what you're really drinking, wherever you are.
A party, a feed, a friend group, a family table. The question for this week isn't only yes or no.
It's who's pouring, and what you leave filled with.

how: Bihagra ki Var is sung in kirtan salok by salok and pauri by pauri; the Sikh Rehat Maryada asks Sikhs to avoid alcohol and other intoxicants.

games.q: the two cups — tap the pairs.
p: filled with nectar in the sangat

s: the saloks headed 'Mardana' use wine as a picture
desire's wine poured by ego, or love's nectar in good company.
Mardana's saloks say drinking with friends brings you closer to God
the good cup is love, filled with nectar in the true congregation.
Mardana was one of the ten Gurus
tradition remembers him as Guru Nanak's companion and musician; the saloks carry his name in their heading.

games.q: your cousin's new friend group is fun, but every hangout ends with someone mocking someone. nobody's drinking. by ang 553, what's worth noticing?
o: who's pouring, and what that company fills him with.
nothing; no alcohol, so the saloks don't apply.
drop every friend; the saloks say company always ruins you.
games.why: the saloks aren't only about alcohol. ego can pour desire and anger in any company; in good company the cup of love fills instead.

practice: Think of one place this week where someone else will be pouring: a party, a group chat, a feed.

Name what you want to keep in your cup, what might crowd it out, and one small plan for when it does, then sit with that plan for the rest of the time. If you'd like, read the saloks on ang 553 first.

carryVoice: Mardana's saloks: two cups, and the question of who's pouring yours. Go gently this weekend, wherever you are.
